correctness.rationale: The reconstructed nonempty face counts are (18,117,336,418,184,12). Replaying the stated toggle order on a vertex-deletion enumeration and sorting the entire directed Hasse graph gave 537 pairs and only one critical vertex and ten critical 3-cells. Forman's theorem gives an ordinary homotopy equivalence to a wedge of ten S^3: all the 3-cells attach to the sole vertex. The sharp flag lower bound 2d+2 follows on vertex-minimal supports by the deletion–star exact sequence and exclusion of universal vertices. At equality each vertex has one nonneighbor, and flagness gives the crosspolytope boundary. For d=3 the eight vertices are eight graph edges in four mutually disjoint two-edge paths. Independent recursion covering the least uncovered graph vertex gave exactly 39 distinct supports. All 39 signed cycles have zero boundary. Subtracting paired 4-cell boundaries in Hasse-topological order leaves only critical and matched-upper degree-three coordinates; the latter have a unit triangular down-boundary block of size 236. Thus a cycle whose critical coordinates vanish is a boundary, and all 184 degree-four boundaries project to zero. The ten stated classes have determinant -1, proving the coordinate lattice is all of Z^10. All 39 vectors have gcd one. A complete distance-preserving automorphism search found eight group elements and orbit representatives (0,1,2,3,4,5,11,17,21) with the stated sizes. Exact Smith forms verified all ranks; only the orbit of carrier 1 has a nonunit invariant factor, 3, giving index 3. This distinguishes integral saturation from rational rank without a finite-field extrapolation.
residual_risks: A finite calculation for the indicated LCF graph and carrier indexing, not a theorem about the number of facets in unrestricted representing cycles.

Independent face, basis and lattice calculations
value.rationale: The Bidiakis cube is a classical cubic graph, and the question of which smallest induced spheres generate a matching complex's integral homology is intrinsic to the graph. Here two eight-element orbits of the same rank have different saturation indices. The index-three example shows exactly how individually primitive classes can fail to generate a saturated lattice despite full rational span in their subspace. The census and explicit basis make the example usable without guessing carriers or relying on rational data.
residual_risks: No broader graph-family claim; the value is the exact integral example and classification.
